- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk premium or market panic.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price by 1–3% in 70% of cases with high sentiment volatility — apply a +1% bias to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3 in 3 consecutive days.
- If sentiment history shows “recovery” pattern (e.g., 0.3→0.7→0.9→0.5), model often misses late-stage rally; add 0.5–1% to forecast at 10–15 day horizon.
